name: Glucose
kicker: Simple sugar cells break down for energy · The body’s main fuel
briefing: Glucose is a simple sugar that serves as the body’s main source of energy, broken down inside cells during a process called glycolysis. Plants build it directly during photosynthesis, while animals get it by digesting carbohydrates like starch and rely on insulin to usher it from the blood into cells. Too much glucose lingering in the blood, as in diabetes, can damage organs over time.

tossups.p: The Cori cycle regenerates this compound in the liver from lactic acid made by working muscles. German chemist Emil Fischer worked out this molecule’s exact structure and stereochemistry, and as a “reducing sugar,” it turns Benedict’s solution brick-red in a classic chemistry test.
tossups.r: Hexokinase attaches a phosphate to this molecule in the first step of glycolysis, which splits it into two molecules of pyruvate. For 10 points, name this simple sugar, the body’s main fuel, with the formula C6H12O6.

tossups.p: German chemist Andreas Marggraf first isolated this compound from raisins in 1747. Rising levels of this molecule trigger beta cells in the pancreas’s Islets of Langerhans to release more insulin, and a dangerous buildup of ketones called ketoacidosis can follow when its levels climb uncontrolled.
tossups.r: Plants make this molecule directly during photosynthesis, combining carbon dioxide and water using sunlight. For 10 points, name this simple sugar that cells break down for energy, abbreviated C6H12O6.

tossups.p: Starch and glycogen chain this molecule together using “alpha” links, while cellulose instead uses “beta” links that the human body cannot digest. A three-month running average of this molecule’s level in the blood is estimated by the hemoglobin A1c test.
tossups.r: Chronically high levels of it in the blood are the hallmark of diabetes, a condition insulin normally helps prevent by moving it into cells. For 10 points, name this sugar with the chemical formula C6H12O6.

tossups.p: Two linked units of this molecule make the disaccharide maltose, while linking it to galactose instead produces lactose. This compound usually curls into a six-sided ring shape once dissolved in water, and the Cori cycle regenerates it in the liver from muscle-derived lactic acid.
tossups.r: Animals store extra amounts by chaining it into glycogen, mainly in the liver and muscles, while plants instead chain it into starch or rigid cellulose. For 10 points, name this simple sugar that fuels cellular respiration.

tossups.p: Starch, glycogen, and cellulose are all built from chains of this molecule, though cellulose’s “beta” links make it indigestible to humans, unlike the “alpha” links in the other two. Hexokinase phosphorylates this compound in the opening step of glycolysis.

trap.title: Glucose, or blood sugar level?
trap.body: Several real tossups with almost identical clues about insulin, the Islets of Langerhans, and the hemoglobin A1c test actually want “blood sugar level,” a measured quantity, rather than this molecule itself. That happens when every clue describes a rising or falling amount rather than the molecule’s own structure or chemistry.
trap.fix: If clues describe the molecule’s structure, formula, or how it is built or broken down (photosynthesis, glycolysis, starch, cellulose), this sugar is the safe answer. If every clue is about a number going up or down in the blood, consider that “blood sugar level” might be the more precise answer wanted.
trap.line: Real answer line: Glucose (accept dextrose, D-glucose; prompt on sugar, monosaccharide, or blood sugar) — a closely related real tossup instead wants “blood sugar level” specifically.
